metric_glossary.reads_as: How often this combination appears at all.
metric_glossary.watch_out: Low support means the estimate rests on few baskets and is unstable.

metric_glossary.reads_as: Given A, how often does B appear?
metric_glossary.watch_out: Inflated whenever B is popular; never rank on this alone.

metric_glossary.reads_as: How many times more likely is B given A than in general?
metric_glossary.watch_out: Lift 1.0 means independence. Unstable when P(B) is tiny.
Favours frequent pairs; complements lift rather than replacing it.

metric_glossary.reads_as: How much more often A appears without B than expected by chance.
metric_glossary.watch_out: Diverges to infinity as confidence approaches 1.

metric_glossary.reads_as: Bounded in [-1, 1]; negative means the items substitute.
metric_glossary.watch_out: Less familiar to stakeholders; useful precisely because it is signed.

why_lift_over_confidence: Confidence P(B|A) is high whenever B is common, regardless of A. Lift divides by P(B), so it isolates dependence. A rule with 90% confidence and lift 1.0 tells you nothing you did not already know from B's base rate.
